title: Parity-Based Reachability Analysis
approach_explanation: Every long step adds 2 to either the x-coordinate or the y-coordinate. Therefore, any number of long steps preserves the parity of both coordinates (starting from (0, 0), both coordinates remain even). The short step allows adding 1 to either the x-coordinate or the y-coordinate exactly once during the entire journey. Taking a short step in the x-direction changes the x-coordinate's parity from even to odd, while keeping the y-coordinate's parity even. Conversely, taking a short step in the y-direction makes the y-coordinate odd while keeping the x-coordinate even. It is fundamentally impossible for both coordinates to end up with odd parities because only one short step is allowed. Thus, if both x and y are odd, it is impossible to reach (x, y), yielding 'NO'. Otherwise, it is always possible, yielding 'YES'.

code_breakdown.explanation: Reads the number of test cases $t$ to execute the query loop.
For each query, reads coordinates $x$ and $y$. Evaluates whether both $x$ and $y$ are odd. If `x % 2 != 0 && y % 2 != 0`, prints 'NO'; otherwise, prints 'YES'.

complexity_analysis.time_justification:
Each testcase performs a constant number of arithmetic operations and conditional checks, taking $O(1)$ time per test case. For $t$ test cases, the total time complexity is $O(t)$, which is $O(1)$ given $t 
eq O(	ext{large})$ or simply $O(t)$.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: The algorithm only uses a few primitive integer variables to store the inputs $t$, $x$, and $y$, resulting in $O(1)$ auxiliary space.

strengths: Extremely concise and optimal time/space complexity.
Direct mathematical reduction of the problem constraints.
edge_cases_handled: Handles minimum and maximum boundary coordinates ($1 \le x, y \le 10$).
Handles fully even coordinates (e.g., reaching via long steps only).

optimization_and_alternatives.tradeoffs: Using bitwise operations like `(x & 1) && (y & 1)` can be slightly faster micro-optimistically, though functionally identical to modulo operators.
